title: Help center
subtitle: Documentation, frequently asked questions and support
methodologyQuestion: Want to see how we analyse and where the data comes from?
learnText: The Documentation tab explains what each module does today and how to use it, with links to the methodology and sources.
supportText: Support is by email and is handled by the person who maintains the project. Response times are not guaranteed.
sourcedText: Research figures show their source and date. When verifiable data is missing, the app marks it as not available instead of making it up.
docsSubtitle: A practical guide per module: what the app does today and how to use it.
contactNoEmail: Questions or suggestions? The contact channel will be published here.

item0.title: Research
item0.text: A page per ticker: canonical financial facts, traceable metrics, thesis, moat, peers, valuation and a chat with sources.

item1.title: Long-term model
item1.text: Fundamental model with visible assumptions (growth, FCF margin, WACC), Bear/Base/Bull scenarios with their spreads, owner earnings, TAM/SAM/SOM and reverse DCF. The «Model» tab of the company page.

item2.title: Portfolio
item2.text: Positions, transactions, import from IBKR and breakdown by sector and currency.

item3.title: Exposures
item3.text: Weights, concentration (top 1 and top 5) and exposure by sector and factor. It does not calculate VaR, drawdown or volatility: these are portfolio-structure metrics.

item4.title: Screener
item4.text: A universe of large caps with real profiles and prices, to start from verifiable candidates.

item5.title: ProPicks
item5.text: Scores from 0 to 100 with auditable reasons (each reason shows its metric and value) and a per-strategy backtest against the S&P 500.

item6.title: Alerts
item6.text: Signals with an explicit materiality threshold, linked to the company page.

item7.title: Insider
item7.text: Trades by insiders (SEC Form 4) with signals for buying clusters.

item8.title: Library and search
item8.text: A library of investing principles and a semantic index rebuilt from Postgres.

item9.title: Watchlist
item9.text: Tracking of symbols with a direct link to their research page.

item10.title: Methodology
item10.text: Valuation engines with their assumptions, data sources, limits (look-ahead, partial coverage) and explicit costs.

item0.question: How much does GerarAI cost?
item0.answer: The app is free to use: it does not have paid plans or charge anything. It runs on free-tier data providers (Finnhub, Yahoo Finance, SEC EDGAR), which limits the coverage and freshness of some data.

item1.question: Is this financial advice?
item1.answer: It is not. GerarAI is an analysis tool: models and theses depend on visible assumptions and can be wrong. Investment decisions are yours.

item2.question: How do I follow a company?
item2.answer: Open its page in Research and press «Follow», next to the name. The symbols you follow are collected in your watchlist.

item3.question: What should I do if I find a bug or have a suggestion?
item3.answer: Write to the address in the Contact tab, with the page and what you expected to see. A response time is not guaranteed.

item4.question: Is market data real-time?
item4.answer: Not real-time. Market data is delayed in most markets: it is meant for analysis, not intraday trading. In the watchlist and research, each price shows the date of its close.

steps.modelText: choose the company, open the «Model» tab and press «Generate model». Review the assumptions (growth, FCF margin, WACC) and the Bear/Base/Bull scenarios with their spreads before trusting the number.
steps.thesisText: Generate the thesis from the same page: hypothesis, scenarios with probabilities, dated catalysts and what would invalidate it. The memo and the EPUB are exported from the thesis view itself («Export memo» and «Export EPUB»);
steps.exportText: is the yearly export of the journal.
steps.decisionText: Record the decision in the Decision journal (Buy / Hold / Trim / Sell / Watch / Avoid) with the evidence behind it and the verifiable conditions («What must be true»). Later, «Expectations vs reality» compares your forecast with the published facts.

glossary.text: Technical terms (DCF, WACC, reverse DCF, moat, margin of safety, look-ahead, owner earnings, TAM/SAM/SOM, ROIC, VaR, drawdown, Sharpe) carry a tooltip with their definition wherever they appear.
